## The idea

A lot of engineering is a loop. Change something, measure it, keep it if it is better, undo it if it isn't, and try the next idea. **Autoresearch** hands that loop to AI agents, so it runs through the night, on many ideas at once, without you.

The hard part is trusting the results. An agent asked to make a number go up will sometimes make it only look higher: it skips the slow case, moves the timer, or just reports a win. So in Thermite, agents only propose. A separate program, the **judge**, builds each change, runs it against the best version so far on the same hardware, checks that its output is still right, and decides. The agents can neither read the judge nor change it.

## What you can point it at

Each campaign is one of three kinds, called **modes**:

<CardGrid>
  <Card title="Make it faster: a hill climb" icon="rocket">
    Push one number, such as speed, size or accuracy, as far as it will go, with guards so that
    nothing else gets worse. *For example: a faster matrix multiply on your GPU.* It runs until you
    stop it. [Try one](tutorials/agents-with-a-free-model.md).
  </Card>
  <Card title="Make it work: a goal campaign" icon="approve-check">
    List what the result must do, as checks: it builds, it loads the model, its answers match.
    Agents work until every check passes. *For example: support a new quantized format.*
    [Try one](tutorials/first-goal-campaign.md).
  </Card>
  <Card title="Find out: a research campaign" icon="magnifier">
    Ask a question. Agents read the web and record claims with quotes, and code checks every quote,
    word for word, against the page it came from. It ends once a review panel finds every question
    answered, or once its research stops adding, with a report built on checked sources.
    *For example: which papers improve 2-bit decoding?*
  </Card>
  <Card title="Or combine them" icon="puzzle">
    Research first, then change the code: a hill climb or a goal campaign can read what a research
    campaign found. [Choose a campaign mode](how-to/campaigns/choose-a-mode.md) helps you pick.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

## How a campaign runs

<Steps>

1. **You set the goal.** On the dashboard, or from a script or your own AI assistant, say what to improve and how to measure it: where the project is, which files the agents may change, and a **kit** that builds, runs and checks it. The **New campaign** page can write a simple kit from your answers.

2. **Agents try ideas side by side.** Each agent works in its own **lane**, on its own copy of the code. A planner gives each lane a different experiment from one shared queue, so the search stays wide. Every agent session starts fresh from the run's records, so a crash loses nothing.

3. **The judge decides.** It builds each change and measures it against the best version so far, on the same device. A change that looks better must hold up again before it counts: on fresh runs, and on test cases the agents never saw when the campaign has them.

4. **Wins become the new starting point.** The best confirmed version is the **champion**, and the next ideas build on it. A change that loses is kept too, with the judge's reasons.

5. **You watch, steer and take the result.** Follow each agent live, add ideas, send the agents a message or pause the run. When you are happy, download the champion as a patch for your project.

</Steps>

## Why you can trust the results

- **Agents never grade their own work.** They submit a change and what they expect it to do. Only the judge's measurement counts.
- **The judge holds the clock.** In a hill climb it first measures where the run starts, and holds every later change against it. It times each change and the champion in alternating blocks on the same device, decides with statistics, and times the champion against itself once a day to learn how noisy the machine is.
- **A surprising win gets a second look.** On a rig with an auditor, an unusually large gain is audited before it is kept. You can also ask to approve every new champion yourself.
- **You can watch it catch cheats.** Thermite's own smoke check submits a dozen changes whose right verdicts are known: a real speed-up, a no-op, a timer edit, a fallback to the reference code, NaN output, memory and disk exhaustion, and an attempt to overwrite the champion. Each must get its expected verdict. [Your first run](tutorials/first-run.md) shows it on your computer.

[Why agents never judge](explanation/why-agents-never-judge.md) follows a change through every step.

## What you get

<CardGrid>
  <Card title="It keeps going" icon="clock">
    Nothing stops a campaign by default: no limit on turns, attempts, failures or time. A goal
    campaign ends when its goals are met, and a research campaign when its questions are answered or its research stops adding.
    Set a
    [budget or a stop time](how-to/campaigns/budget-and-stop-time.md) when you want one.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Your machines, your models" icon="laptop">
    Run it on your own computer, on machines with GPUs, on a Kubernetes cluster, or on a RunPod GPU
    by the hour. The agents use a free model, a model server of your own, an API key, or a Claude or
    ChatGPT subscription.
  </Card>
  <Card title="One place to watch and steer" icon="analytics">
    One dashboard shows every campaign on every machine, live. A REST API and MCP give your scripts
    and your own AI assistant the same view and the same controls. Only you approve what matters.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Nothing is forgotten" icon="notes">
    Every attempt is kept with its verdict, and the agents keep field notes as they work. Each
    campaign's records go into a [knowledge base](explanation/journals-and-knowledge.md) that later
    runs can read.
  </Card>
</CardGrid>

## Under the hood

Thermite has two kinds of part. **Control** is the one place you watch and steer from. **Rigs** do the research, each on its own machine, cluster node or cloud pod, and each rig is two containers: a **harness**, where the agents and the judge work, and a **supervisor**, which links the rig to control and runs its advisors.

<HowItWorks />

### A run, step by step

1. **You start a campaign** on control: from **New campaign** on the dashboard, over the REST API or MCP, or with the `thermite` command line. Its **contract** says what counts: a number to push up in a **hill climb**, or a list of goals to meet in a **goal** campaign (see [Campaign modes](explanation/campaign-modes.md)). Its **kit** says how to build and measure your project. Control sends the rig you choose a signed command to start the run.
2. **The rig takes it.** The supervisor takes the signed command from control's message bus, fetches the project, the kit and any model files the command names, each by its commit or its hash, and hands the command to the harness. The harness checks the signature, and that what was fetched is what the command named.
3. **The planner hands out the work.** The run has one **experiment queue**, a list of what to try. At the start of each round, the planner gives each **lane** its next experiment, and a starting point: the champion, or the lane's own best result. No two lanes get the same experiment.
4. **A worker tries it.** Each **trial** is a fresh agent session, which the harness builds from its records: the experiment, the lane's recent results with the judge's reasons, and the campaign's brief. The worker changes its own copy of the code, may test it in runs that never count, and submits one change with what it expects it to do.
5. **The judge decides.** It builds the change and runs the kit's check on it. In a hill climb, it then times the change against the champion on the same device, in alternating blocks; in a goal campaign, it checks each goal. A change that looks better is measured again on fresh runs, and on hidden test cases when the contract has them, before it counts. No agent can read or change the judge.
6. **A confirmed win becomes the champion,** the code that the next trials build on. When the campaign calls for an audit, the auditor's clear is the last step. When you asked to decide yourself, the win waits for you under **Needs you**.
7. **The advisors steer.** The teachers read the results and the champion's code, add ideas to the queue and give the planner rules, each with its reasons. The review panel scores goals that code can't measure. The advisors never set a verdict.
8. **Everything is recorded, and reaches you.** The rig's **ledger** keeps every experiment, attempt, measurement and verdict. The supervisor sends it all to control, where you follow the run on **Live** and its page, and steer it with signed commands: pause it, message its agents, add experiments. It pushes the results to git, and control files each campaign's records in its collection of the knowledge base, for later runs to read.
9. **Round after round,** until the goals are met, a budget or stop time you set runs out, or you stop it. Nothing stops a campaign by default.

The third mode, **research**, has no project to change and no kit. Its workers read sources through the rig's archiving fetcher and record claims with exact quotes. Code finds every quote, word for word, in the archived page before a claim counts. Once the review panel finds every question answered, its research stops adding, or its maximum duration is up, the run ends with its final report, led by a research paper that code checks.

[How the parts fit together](explanation/how-it-fits-together.md) explains each part, [Agents, lanes and the planner](explanation/agents-lanes-planner.md) a trial, [Why agents never judge](explanation/why-agents-never-judge.md) the judge, and [Supervision](explanation/supervision.md) the advisors.

## Try it

You need Linux or macOS, Docker or Podman, and about twenty minutes. No GPU, no paid model and no account: the first tutorials use a free model, or none.

Thermite is young and changes every day. Its agents run the code that a model writes on your computer, so read [Known limits](reference/known-limits.md) before you give it a model.

## Join the community

Thermite's community meets on the **Hackers in the Loop** Discord. Ask a question, share what your campaigns found, and see what is being built next. Bugs and feature requests go in [GitHub issues](https://github.com/iammrduncan/thermite/issues).

## For agents

The whole site is available to AI agents as plain text: [`llms.txt`](/llms.txt) lists every page, and [`llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) holds all of them in one file. Every page is also published as Markdown at its own address with `.md` added.
